clue.text: We hear the Inland Revenue people are in stitches

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the business is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.words: the Inland Revenue people are in
parts.note: the business Britain's old Inland Revenue was in was collecting tax

explanation.surface: Tax officials are said to be laughing uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In stitches' looks like a phrase for laughing; 'stitches' alone is the definition, and 'are in' tells you what trade the officials work in. The Inland Revenue was Britain's tax collector.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacks are long loose temporary stitches used in sewing to hold fabric in place.

clue.text: End of acceptable behaviour?

parts.note: read 'end' as the aim or goal: the standard that polite behaviour aims at, the conventionally correct way to act, which also looks like a finished item

explanation.surface: A question about where good manners stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' seems to mean a stopping point, but here it means an objective, like 'the end justifies the means'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names whatever social convention regards as correct conduct, the goal of acceptable manners.

clue.text: Tune Oscar composed for a one-time lover

indicators.note: composed suggests music being written, so these letters are arranged into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer writes a song for a former sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges TUNE and OSCAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a historical paid mistress of wealthy men, a lover kept for a time.

clue.text: Celebrity is given one in flight

indicators.note: in tells us the numeral one is placed inside the word for a celebrity

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A famous person is handed a seat on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside STAR. 'Flight' looks like air travel but means a run of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair, in the collective sense, is a whole series of steps, exactly what a flight of steps is.

clue.text: Winter transport for the Crazy Boot gang

indicators.note: crazy says these letters are wildly disordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sledge meant for a wild gang called the Boot gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges BOOT GANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a long light sledge used for sliding down snowy slopes in winter.

clue.text: Group loyalty shown when party returned is in good shape

indicators.note: in puts the reversed party and the word is inside the word for good shape

parts.note: to be in trim is to be in good shape

indicators.note: returned means the word for the party is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Loyalty to one's own grows when a party wins again and is healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LAB into BAL; with IS that goes 'in' TRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong loyalty to one's own social group above all others.

clue.text: Inclination to take a chance about name

indicators.note: about means the betting word goes around the abbreviation for name

parts.note: to take a chance is to bet

explanation.surface: A tendency to gamble on a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BET around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural tendency or leaning toward something.

clue.text: Young pig served with decoration of the highest quality

parts.note: a gilt is a young female pig
something given a decorative border has been edged

explanation.surface: A piglet brought to the table with a garnish is top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: A gilt is a farming term for a young sow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged describes the safest, best-grade securities, hence anything of the highest quality.

clue.text: Beer is in the passage

indicators.note: in means the word is goes inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Beer has been spilt in the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beer is in' reads as a pub sentence; 'is' is literal fodder and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves.

clue.text: Teacher to note: old money is in a lot of trouble

parts.note: E is a musical note
a ducat was an old gold coin used across Europe

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher learns that old money has caused a great deal of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a lot of trouble' reads as one phrase, but 'is in a lot' is the fodder and 'trouble' the anagram signal, making IONALIST. A ducat was a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An educationalist is a specialist in education, broadly someone who teaches or theorises teaching.

clue.text: Sauce kept in each container held by servants is packed in ice

indicators.note: packed in means everything so far goes inside the frozen water word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: held by means the servants word surrounds each plus container

parts.note: men can mean male servants or retainers
per means each, as in so much per head
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Sauce stored in containers by staff is kept on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks culinary but means cheek. 'held by' and 'packed in' are the two container signals, nested; 'kept in' is linking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for cheeky rudeness, the same as insolent disrespect.

clue.text: Do without breakfast, largely owing to epidemic

parts.note: without can mean outside, out

indicators.note: largely means only the greater part of the word breakfast is used, its opening letters

explanation.surface: Skipping breakfast mostly because of a disease going round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' keeps BREAK from 'breakfast'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is a sudden occurrence of disease, the start of an epidemic.

clue.text: Get back from uncle and think again

definitions.meaning: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, and you buy back pawned goods from him
split as ..., to deem again, to judge afresh

explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a pawned item is to buy it back; re-deem means judge anew.

clue.text: Welsh rite performed once upon a time

indicators.note: a rite is performed, and here the letters are worked into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old Welsh ceremony was carried out long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges WELSH RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile means former or formerly, of an earlier time.

clue.text: Humorist claims a philosophical influence cut by distant travelling

indicators.note: claims means the humorist takes in and holds the rest

parts.note: a wag is a joker or humorist

indicators.note: cut by means the philosophical word is split open by the word for distant

parts.note: yin is the passive principle in Chinese philosophy
far means distant

explanation.surface: A comic adopts an Eastern doctrine, interrupted from afar while journeying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by' and 'claims' are nested container signals. Yin is the passive principle of Chinese philosophy; 'Humorist' is a joker, not a famous writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayfaring means journeying, especially on foot.

clue.text: Rose ordered to "get in lane"

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Rose is told to get in lane by traffic police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges GET IN LANE. 'Rose' looks like a name or a verb but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose species.

clue.text: Foreman nearly makes a blunder

indicators.note: nearly means the word for foreman loses its final letter

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a foreman or boss

explanation.surface: The boss almost makes a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last R of GAFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing social mistake.

clue.text: Did Noah come in on this?

definitions.text: Did Noah come in on this?

parts.words: Did Noah come in on this?
parts.note: playful question about the biblical deluge: the ark arrived on the incoming rising sea level, or the great water

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about the ark's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: The rising tide and the biblical deluge are merged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the incoming tide when water rises, pictured as the deluge that carried the ark.

clue.text: Convenient hospital with first youngster

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
and means together with

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of youngster

explanation.surface: A nearby hospital that puts young people first.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means conveniently near or useful.

clue.text: Hit back at commercial rubbish, including one that's clumsy

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read in reverse

parts.note: lam is slang for hit or thrash
ad is short for an advertisement or commercial

indicators.note: including means the word for rubbish takes in one

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out at junk advertising and is awkward about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'including' are the reversal and container signals. 'Hit back at' reads as retaliation, but 'at' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means lacking skill, awkward in movement or handling.

clue.text: Trance-inducing drink

indicators.note: inducing suggests something brought about or changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink that sends one into a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inducing' rearranges TRANCE; the hyphen hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the mythological drink of the gods, or any delicious drink.

clue.text: Greek character goes to some length in China to get hot spice

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the li is a traditional Chinese unit of distance

explanation.surface: A Greek travels far across China in search of a fiery seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' seems to be a place to go but is part of a description of the Chinese unit LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chili is the hot pepper, or the spicy powder made from it.

clue.text: Lighten the peacekeepers' 26

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces
the answer to 26 across is a musical subject, and a burden is the refrain or main idea of a song

explanation.surface: Ease the load carried by the peacekeeping troops.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the other clue whose answer means a refrain; burden is that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To unburden is to relieve of a load, to make lighter.

clue.text: Slow girl taking exercises

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
PT is physical training, school exercises

explanation.surface: A sluggish girl does her workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt can mean slow to learn, dull.

clue.text: A craggy formation on the skin?

definitions.text: A craggy formation on the skin?

parts.words: A craggy formation on the skin?
parts.note: the same word names a steep rocky outcrop and a mark left on the body by a healed wound

explanation.surface: A rugged feature appearing on someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: A craggy cliff and a healed wound share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is both a rocky cliff (in northern English place names) and a mark from a wound.

clue.text: Hell at home: Eastwood embracing a cowgirl showing new reluctance

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
in means at home

indicators.note: embracing means the actor's first name holds the letter a

parts.note: Clint Eastwood, the western film actor
Io was a maiden turned into a heifer in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Hell at home as Clint Eastwood hugs a ranch girl, all reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts A inside CLINT. The cowgirl is not a ranch hand but Io, whom Zeus changed into a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinclination is an unwillingness or reluctance to do something.

clue.text: Would one fish by the lake dressed in these?

definitions.text: Would one fish by the lake dressed in these?

parts.note: the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Would anyone go fishing by a lake wearing underwear?
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, which is what the question asks about.

clue.text: Musical passage for beginners to tell how each movement ends

indicators.note: beginners signals taking the first letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A guide to the opening of a symphony, explaining how its parts conclude.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a principal melodic subject in a musical work.
